items.text: On Linux the Settings window has the Mac's pages, with switches, drop-downs, number fields and a shell picker.
On Linux the Settings window edits list settings as chips you can add to and remove.
On Linux the Settings Font row is a menu of the installed fixed-width fonts, as on the Mac.
On Linux, Settings > Advanced shows the config file, its backups with Restore, and the change toast with Undo, as on the Mac.
Settings > Shell offers Git Bash and one entry per WSL distro, and each pick opens that shell.
The 16th pane open at once keeps the fast drawing path: the D3D11 device is now a pool.
